ranked.headline: Models infer single-cell molecular state from H&E, spatial spots and multi-omics
ranked.summary: New preprints treat routine H&E and multicellular spatial spots as recoverable single-cell molecular readouts, alongside larger cell foundation models.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is computational recovery of single-cell molecular state from tissue measurements. Three preprints treat H&E as a molecular readout. Loki2, trained on 15 million cells, tests how much molecular and cellular state routine histology encodes. GenVinci reconstructs 3D molecular tissue scenes and maps senescence across aging mouse organs and human skin. sc-HistoMorphomics links 194 nuclear morphometric features to spatial transcriptomics. Spatial methods also reach cellular and subcellular resolution. st2sc infers single-cell expression from multicellular spots. A rotation-equivariant network learns 3D subcellular transcript embeddings. CIRCA recovers identifiable cell and niche programs tied to plaque pathology. Representation learning continues to scale. Bloom unifies expression and chromatin accessibility across 300,000 mouse brain cells. MCT models cell sets to learn gene co-regulation. scUNVEIL pretrains on about 92 million human cells via next-UMI prediction. A secondary strand targets perturbation and dynamics. GFM predicts responses to unseen Perturb-seq perturbations, DRAFT infers dynamic GRNs along multi-omics trajectories, and CIRCE infers graded signaling strength.

ranked.headline: Automation and cross-modal registration scale single-cell and tissue-level neural mapping
ranked.summary: New preprints pair automated Patch-seq, atlas-based neuron identification and whole-organ segmentation with imaging–mass spectrometry coregistration.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is scaling quantitative cell characterization by combining automation with multimodal registration. In Patch-seq, detergent-cleaned reusable pipettes, robotic nucleus extraction and sonication preserve electrophysiology and transcriptomic yield, laying groundwork for automated profiling. Probabilistic C. elegans head-neuron atlases built from near-wild-type strains reach 86.3% top-1 variability-aware identification. Whole-bulb light-sheet expansion microscopy with automated segmentation maps thousands of glomeruli in intact mouse olfactory bulbs. SCOUBI infers axon-dendrite interfaces from extrasomatic transcripts in mouse brain spatial transcriptomics. A second strand integrates imaging modalities: MeXalign coregisters LA-ICP-TOFMS and immunofluorescence via segmentation masks, and FluoMALDI links fluorescence-defined genes, proteins and organelles to spatial lipid composition. Disease- and glia-focused tools add 3D readouts. PASTA resolves amyloid-beta lesion heterogeneity, growth lineages and microglial contacts, and PolyMorph3D quantifies microglia morphology with up to four-marker colocalization. Stitched montage cryo-ET of lamellipodial Arp2/3 actin networks is methodologically related but lies outside neural tissue.

ranked.headline: Nucleic-acid foundation models specialize by taxon and molecule, and move into regulatory design
ranked.summary: New preprints extend DNA and RNA foundation models to parasite genomes, modified bases, ncRNA, and constrained enhancer design, with diagnostic benchmarking.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is specialization of nucleic-acid foundation models beyond generic DNA pretraining. On the genomic side, an apicomplexan-specific model pretrained on 455 assemblies improves regulatory signal prediction in the small, data-sparse Plasmodium falciparum genome, while ModBERT conditions pretraining on population variants and long-read CpG methylation to predict chromatin features and variant effects. Evaluation is becoming diagnostic rather than leaderboard-driven: LAMP dissects why post-training sequence-to-function models on personal genomes fails to improve expression prediction, implicating distal sequence, and fine-tuned Borzoi and AlphaGenome are benchmarked against variant-based predictors for whole-blood expression in admixed Latino individuals. A parallel RNA track adds B-RANKO's bidirectional decoder-only ncRNA generator, LncRFM's structure-guided masking across 24.7M lncRNAs, and MARRI's mechanism-aware encoding of opening penalties and hybridization gains. Design is likewise constrained: GENECraft couples a genomic language model to a functional oracle without training, and REGAL programs enhancer grammar via reinforcement learning with cross-species validation.

ranked.headline: ROS and redox chemistry act through defined protein modules in plant stress and development
ranked.summary: New Arabidopsis, apple and pear studies map ROS, H2S and peroxiredoxin effects onto specific kinases, transcription factors, desaturases and splicing factors.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is redox chemistry acting through defined protein modules rather than as nonspecific damage. In Arabidopsis, peroxisomal H2O2 homeostasis under PEG-induced water stress rebalances ABA and GA metabolism to slow seed germination. 2-Cys peroxiredoxins interact with the omega-3 desaturases FAD7/FAD8, increasing trienoic fatty acids in phosphatidylglycerol and aiding PSII recovery from high-light photoinhibition. H2S persulfidation and PRMT5-dependent LSm4 methylation link H2S signaling to alternative splicing during stomatal closure. In apple, MxMPK4-1 phosphorylates NADP-malic enzyme MxME3-7 at S201, enhancing ROS signaling and iron-deficiency tolerance. In pear, PUB8 targets ZAT11/12 for degradation, while ZAT11/12 activate LAC1 to drive ROS-linked lignin polymerization during stone cell formation. Related work covers ursolic acid control of ascorbate via MdMYB70/MdbHLH62, MdGGP2 and MdAPX1 in fresh-cut apple, and melatonin plus selenium nanoparticles alleviating soybean salt stress through MAPK-related transcription, hormones and lipid remodeling. A superoxide dismutase review provides historical context.

ranked.headline: Defined regulators sustain germline gene expression, transposon silencing and gamete fitness
ranked.summary: New preprints link COPS5, meiotic stress factors and HLH-30/TFEB to piRNA silencing, gamete protection and fertility across mouse, yeast and worm.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how specific regulators sustain gene expression programs and genome integrity during gametogenesis. In mouse germ cells, COPS5 loss downregulates piRNA pathway genes, reduces pachytene piRNAs, derepresses LINE1 and IAP transposons, and arrests spermatogenesis. In budding yeast meiosis, Hsf1, Skn7, Msn2 and Msn4 are active without external stress, and the antioxidant genes TSA1 and AHP1 protect gametes. In C. elegans, HLH-30/TFEB loss shifts the basal transcriptome in stage- and age-dependent ways and lowers sperm and progeny numbers. Separately, disrupting rRNA biogenesis via rpoa-2 causes histone mRNA 3' misprocessing through cell-cycle and genome-surveillance regulators. Drosophila work shows Marf1 integrated into accessory gland regulatory networks and GAR1 linked to sgg splicing and PI3K/AKT signaling. Single-cell and spatial maps implicating HEYL in human ovarian aging, and a yeast mitochondrial-nuclear synthetic genetic array screen implicating Rim101 signaling, extend the scope beyond germline silencing.

ranked.headline: Cell-type and stage-resolved omics map early molecular lesions in neurodegeneration models
ranked.summary: Preprints resolve disease-associated molecular change by cell type, age and stage, from Huntington's models to ALS and GBA1 variants.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is resolving molecular pathology by cell type, age or disease stage. In R6/1 mice, cell-type-resolved proteomics shows synaptic protein loss in excitatory neurons before motor onset, with reduced neuronal-support proteins in glia. TgHD minipig putamen shows age-dependent transcript and protein changes, including reduced D2 neuron markers. Fmr1-KO profiling likewise reports cell type-specific remodelling of excitatory and inhibitory synapses. In ALS-related work, a TDP-43 APEX2 atlas finds interactome changes persisting beyond stress granule clearance, younger ALS donors show higher neuronal somatic mutation burden with an SBS5 signature, and SETX loss has stage-dependent effects in iPSC motor neurons. A multiplexed assay maps function for over 10,400 GBA1 variants, and Ankle2-VRK1 work links proteostasis to neuronal resilience in Drosophila. Not all items address aging or neurodegeneration directly.

ranked.headline: CRISPRi knockdown responses transfer imperfectly across cell lines and cohorts, tracking growth programs
ranked.summary: Two preprints show CRISPRi responses vary by cell line and aging cohort, with proliferation programs confounding rankings and transfer needing partial screening.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how well CRISPRi perturbation effects generalize beyond the context where they were measured. Perturb-seq of essential genes in four human cell lines gives a median cross-line response correlation of 0.52, and prediction in a new line requires screening about 30% of it. A separate analysis finds that CRISPRi rankings for reversing aging expression signatures change with the aging cohort and track cell growth programs, pointing to proliferation as a confounder. The remaining preprints are methodological and do not concern CRISPRi: cross-modal batch correction, spatial imputation (ARC-Impute) and co-localisation testing (spicyR v2), and sequencing assays (Siphon-seq, Catch*ReSeq, nanopore cell-free RNA extraction comparison).

ranked.headline: Omics inferences shift with scoring, depth, composition and replicate noise
ranked.summary: Eight preprints show network, gene-set and cell-state conclusions varying with evaluation depth, scoring, composition and replicates, calling for explicit controls.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that transcriptomic and proteomic conclusions depend on analytical choices and biological context. Co-abundance method rankings change with evaluation depth, and colorectal stress granule fibroblast-epithelial contrasts depend on scoring method and depth. Efferocytosis readouts after stroke are bounded by cell composition and time, and replicate-library variation sets the noise floor for cell-state claims in drug-tolerant PC9 cells, where a library-level permutation test is proposed. Compartment specificity recurs in cochlear ageing, which shows weak systemic concordance and a distinct macrophage programme, and in GABAergic channel expression, which reinforces rather than compensates dendritic conductance load. Cell-state conditioning predicts responses to an unseen stimulus but not stimulus-dependent genetic effects. The new emphasis is on stating depth, scoring and replicate structure before interpreting signals, rather than treating readouts as context-free.

ranked.headline: Context-specific regulatory variant effects are being predicted and mapped onto disease loci
ranked.summary: Sequence models, ancestry-aware expression data and cell-resolved frameworks are refining how regulatory variants are linked to cell states and disease genes.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is assigning regulatory variant effects to defined biological contexts. AlphaGenome 2 predicts cell-type-specific regulatory activity and variant effects from 1-Mb sequence, and ChromBPNet models of 17 hematopoietic types score 302,830 variants with lineage-structured accessibility effects. In admixed individuals, whole-blood RNA-seq links West African ancestry to more allele-specific expression, with 52 ancestry-associated loci replicating. Downstream frameworks apply context to disease loci: CAS-X integrates fine-mapped eQTLs across five metabolic tissues and CELL-X uses islet single-cell transcriptomes for type 2 diabetes. The endometriosis study shows that cell-state prioritization depends on marker definition and donor structure. PrediXSKAT weights rare coding variants by predicted cis-regulated expression. The midkine Mendelian randomization study in pancreatic cancer is only peripheral to this thread.

ranked.headline: Transcriptomics gains longitudinal sampling of living tissue and single-cell isoform-level regulatory resolution
ranked.summary: Preprints add repeated in vivo spatial sampling and joint accessibility-isoform profiling, extending transcriptomic readouts beyond single-timepoint, gene-level snapshots.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is extending transcriptomic resolution in time and transcript structure. LIFE-seq (nanoforest arrays) and LANCE-seq (encoded microneedle arrays) capture spatial RNA from living tissue without terminating it; LIFE-seq follows cortical injury within the same mouse, and LANCE-seq profiles mouse brain and tracks APAP-induced liver injury over time. FULL-seq jointly profiles chromatin accessibility and full-length transcripts in single cells, linking promoter regulation to alternative first exon usage. SpaceMACE adds spatial proximity and expression similarity to tumour-cell annotation, and PDAC BioPortal integrates bulk, single-nucleus and spatial cohorts. The cervical profiling, HPV neuroimmune signature and KDM3B-ErbB cholangiocarcinoma studies apply transcriptomic or epigenetic readouts to specific tissues and diseases rather than adding temporal or isoform resolution.

ranked.headline: Long-read and genome-resolved metagenomics expose microbial diversity missed by short-read and amplicon methods
ranked.summary: HiFi sludge assemblies and 2,698 Great Barrier Reef sediment MAGs show how assembly resolution shapes ecological and functional interpretation of microbiomes.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that resolution of genomic and phylogenetic structure determines ecological interpretation of microbiomes. HiFi long-read metagenomics of activated sludge recovers denitrifiers, nitrifiers and Accumulibacter that short-read assemblies miss, which biases N2O-related inferences. Great Barrier Reef sediments yield 2,698 MAGs, mostly novel, with notable metabolic heterogeneity. Supporting methods include hilldiv3, which unifies neutral, phylogenetic and functional Hill-number analysis, and MiSA, which tests for disease-linked spatial dysbiosis in image-based oral biofilm data. Amplicon-based studies add ecological context: marble subaerial biofilms show taxonomic turnover with conserved phylogenetic structure, octocoral microbiomes are host-specific and stable over three years, and river microeukaryotes track water chemistry. These studies differ in system and method, and only some are genome-resolved.

ranked.headline: Histone methylation pathways restrict silencing to specific loci via defined recruitment, protection and erasure steps
ranked.summary: New studies resolve how H3K4, H3K9 and H3K27 methylation machineries are targeted, shielded or removed at defined loci in development and cell identity.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is locus-restricted silencing through histone methylation across mouse, Arabidopsis, Neurospora, Drosophila and Xenopus. Mechanistic steps are now resolved. H3K4 methylation and DNA methylation cooperate to protect regulatory elements from Polycomb in mouse ES cells. In Arabidopsis, Pol II Ser2P redistribution into gene bodies recruits the FLD-LD H3K4me1 demethylase complex to license silencing. PRC2/H3K27me3 is directed by maternal Foxh1 in Xenopus, shapes PHE1 binding at imprinted genes in endosperm, and depends on CAF-1 in Neurospora facultative heterochromatin. For H3K9, IDC, STWL and PZG recruit SETDB1 via WDE to phf7 in Drosophila, and EHMT1/2 time cortical neurogenesis through H3K9me2-dependent and -independent routes.

ranked.headline: Cell-type-resolved transcriptomic atlases map Alzheimer's disease programs in mouse and human cortex
ranked.summary: Seven preprints add AD mouse and human cell-type datasets, from VIP interneuron rescue to microglial lysosomal programs and cortical miRNA signatures.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is cell-type-resolved omics applied to Alzheimer's disease (AD) models and human brain. A 5xFAD snRNA-seq atlas finds VIP interneurons most disrupted in synapse programs and preferentially rescued by rolipram, implicating a Pde7b/CREB1 cAMP axis. A harmonized collection of 1,863 uniformly processed mouse cortex and hippocampus samples, including AD models, supports cross-study comparison. Lysosomal biogenesis (MiT/TFE) is reported to precede and couple to disease-associated microglia reprogramming across murine injury, amyloidosis and human AD. A 1,738-cortex human meta-analysis links miRNAs, notably miR-132-3p, to tau pathology. Developmental regulatory maps from 231 prefrontal cortices and the VEGABrain tool add developmental context. The preeclampsia miRNA-mRNA study is peripheral to this thread.

ranked.headline: Protein language models are adapted with dynamics, structure and reference inputs for specific tasks
ranked.summary: Seven preprints add dynamics, 3D context, reference modeling or structure-derived profiles to sequence models for variant, PTM, kcat and design tasks.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is specializing sequence representations for defined prediction tasks by supplying task-relevant information that generic embeddings lack. DynamicsPLM adds molecular dynamics heads to a 35M-parameter model for zero-shot variant effect prediction. HieraPTM combines sequence, language model and 3D structure features to progress from PTM site recognition to functional phosphosite prediction. EnzRef models reactants and products separately against a frozen protein language model to predict kcat. Adjacent structure-focused work follows a related logic: FoldMapper uses structure-derived evolutionary profiles for inverse folding, MANTA separates geometric prior estimation from coordinate generation for disordered ensembles, and AbPoolRank selects among mixed antibody-antigen prediction pools (58.0% Success@1). MXfold2 adds chemical probing supervision for RNA secondary structure. These are not all language-model adapters, but they share task-specific augmentation of sequence-only inputs.

ranked.headline: Copy number variation is resolved through long-read genomes, pangenomes and coalescent models
ranked.summary: Pangenome, long-read and coalescent-network studies address gene copy number variation, with simulation benchmarking supporting orthology-based gene family analysis.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is gene copy number variation, addressed through sequence-resolved genomes and model-based inference. A gene-based pangenome of 140 C. elegans strains shows that hyper-divergent regions are enriched for copy-number variable environmental response genes and identifies a novel anthelmintic resistance locus. PacBio HiFi sequencing gives near-complete de novo genomes of recently isolated Malian P. falciparum, with variation in telomere-associated architecture. A coalescent duplication network model infers copy number history from copy counts alone, applied to NB-ARC domain counts of NLR genes. OrthoSimulator offers empirically calibrated simulations with known orthology ground truth, relevant to benchmarking gene family analysis. The phylogeny-localization and ancient DNA relatedness preprints are methodologically distinct and do not address copy number directly.

ranked.headline: Regulators of xylem, root and leaf anatomy tune water transport and stress tolerance in grasses
ranked.summary: Single-cell, spatial and allometric analyses link xylem and root patterning to hydraulics and drought tolerance across wheat, rice and bentgrass.
ranked.synthesis: The items converge on quantitative regulation of organ and vascular anatomy in grasses and its physiological consequences. A xylem single-cell atlas places ZHD3 and ZHD4 at the centre of protoxylem secondary cell wall morphology. In wheat, nodal root anatomy differs by culm position beyond root area scaling, with distinct genetic associations after allometric correction, and metaxylem number is remodelled along root axes, with hydraulic modelling tying vessel patterning to water transport. In rice, OsWOX11 promotes thick AR2 roots, with a higher-activity promoter variant (Hap3), and an RLC3-KNOX module activates lignin genes controlling leaf rolling and drought tolerance. In creeping bentgrass, miR164-NAC dosage separates growth, drought and salt responses via AsNHX1. New here is resolution: cell-type atlases, allometric correction and dosage effects.

ranked.headline: Elicitor perception and immune signaling diversify across peptides, fungal effectors, viral proteins and metabolites
ranked.summary: New work links receptor-level elicitor recognition, NLR-dependent cell death and SAR induction, with a systemin receptor lesion in N. benthamiana LAB.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how plants detect elicitors and convert recognition into immune outputs. In Nicotiana, four new bioactive systemins are perceived by SlSYR1, and a premature stop codon in SYR1 orthologs of LAB N. benthamiana accounts for lineage-specific insensitivity. The Ustilaginoidea virens protein UvWSC1 triggers OsCPK13- and SOBIR1-dependent cell death, whereas SCMV HC-Pro triggers ADR1/NRG1-dependent hypersensitive death modulated by P3N-PIPO, which also affects RNA silencing suppression. N-hydroxypipecolic acid is reported to induce systemic acquired resistance to leaf rust in wheat. In Arabidopsis, UGT74F1 and UGT74F2 restrict turnip mosaic virus independently of salicylic acid, jasmonate and RNA silencing. The mild SCMV vector for maize is a methodological tool and is peripheral to this thread.

ranked.headline: Designed protein binders and glue degraders exploit interfaces and degrons for selective modulation
ranked.summary: Preprints pair structure-guided glue and E3 recruiter design with computational binder and engineered-kinase approaches for selective control of protein function.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is deliberate engineering of protein-protein interfaces to control target fate or activity. Two glue degrader preprints exemplify this: TrIP-MGRD targets transient PPI pockets, supported by a CDK12-DDB1 cryo-EM structure and the glue C432, while a HER2-directed antibody conjugate of a CCNK glue degrader gives HER2-selective cyclin K degradation. A degron-informed study establishes DCAF10 as a degradation E3 ligase, using an optimized Pr-GFI recruiter against FKBP12 and BRD9. Computational design appears in latent-space PDZ-binding peptide design, including off-target-aware and dual-target design, and in MobGen monobodies against the SARS-CoV-2 Spike RBD. Paired Lck deep mutational scanning yields a nilotinib-sensitized variant. The shift is toward rational, selective, interface-aware design, though the items differ in modality and maturity.

ranked.headline: Omics and drug-response models are stress-tested for noise and cross-dataset generalization
ranked.summary: Preprints show that cross-source and cross-modality validation exposes limits that single-cohort benchmarks conceal in omics and drug-response modelling.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that quantitative omics models are judged by robustness to noise and to dataset shift rather than by within-cohort accuracy. A comparison of six drug-perturbation transcriptomic resources finds high treated-expression agreement but limited cross-source concordance of drug-induced responses. In glioblastoma, CTGAN and TVAE augmentation of a 38-patient circulating miRNA cohort did not generalize across plasma and tissue cohorts, so same-modality validation overstates performance. Method preprints address noise directly: Elflow combines automated QC with self-supervised representations for cytometry, DeepCINET models viability assay noise in drug-response ranking, and BI-SCUDO Regression is a rank-based survival predictor reported to outperform LASSO, Random Forest and XGBoost on TCGA cohorts. PTM-BDL adds site-resolved phosphosite features to drug-response prediction.

ranked.headline: Multiomic profiling resolves stromal cell states and conserved matrix-remodelling programmes across tissues
ranked.summary: Single-nucleus and cross-organ datasets now define stromal state continuity and a conserved fibrosis core, linking fibroblast regulators to matrix remodelling.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the definition of stromal cell states and the matrix-remodelling programmes they carry. In human atrial fibrillation, single-nucleus multi-omics resolves fibroblast and cardiomyocyte states and implicates JMJD1C in TGF-beta-driven fibroblast remodelling. Paired bulk, single-nucleus RNA and chromatin accessibility profiling of healthy synovium and infrapatellar fat pad describes a continuous stromal landscape rather than discrete types. Cross-organ analysis of human and mouse fibrosis RNA-seq identifies a conserved 25-gene matrix-remodelling core, though gene-level cross-species concordance is weak. HIPPO competency signatures and oxidative metabolism mark human stromal clones with high bone-forming capacity. The heart isoform atlas and bovine MSC culture transcriptomics address adjacent questions of isoform-level change and culture-dependent adaptation, and do not directly examine stromal matrix control.

ranked.headline: Drosophila and stickleback studies link rapid adaptation to thermal and predator cues
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published study test how thermal, seasonal and insecticide pressures shape adaptive divergence in Drosophila and stickleback.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the genomic basis of rapid adaptive change in ectotherms facing thermal, seasonal, chemical and predation pressures. A preprint on the pest fly Drosophila suzukii tests whether seasonal adaptive tracking, linked to thermal tolerance evolution and seasonal allele frequency shifts, contributes to invasion success. Pooled sequencing of 12 replicate experimental-evolution populations identifies genomic regions under selection in divergent chronotypes. An outdoor insecticide experiment reports that half of the populations went extinct despite strong parallel polygenic adaptation, and pre-adaptation is examined in relation to these outcomes. In Icelandic threespine stickleback adapted to geothermal warming, transgenerational and within-generation plasticity show distinct genetic architectures. A published stickleback study shows that paternal predation cues alter early gene expression in sons and daughters through distinct pathways. What is new is the separation of plasticity components and the explicit linkage of genomic trajectories to contingent evolutionary outcomes.

ranked.headline: Mitochondrial and organelle architecture shifts with age, stress and gene loss
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and one published study link organelle remodeling, mitochondrial redox genetics and mtDNA heteroplasmy detection.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is mitochondrial and organelle architecture as a readout of cell state. In living adult C. elegans, MoMA maps six organelles across somatic cells and reports an abrupt midlife architectural state shift. A separate C. elegans ultrastructural study shows that mitochondria remodel during germ cell differentiation and oxidative stress, forming fzo-1-dependent protective morphotypes. At the genetic level, a frameshift deletion disabling the mitochondrial redox enzyme GLRX2 underlies somersaulting in domestic pigeons, with mouse and zebrafish models addressing the phenotype. Single-molecule FISH protocols for mtDNA variants, deletions and haplotypes in human and Drosophila cells extend this framework to quantifying heteroplasmy. The published FLP recombinase study does not share this thread directly; it reports that high multicopy FLP expression disrupts synaptic protein trafficking in C. elegans, a separate caution for transgenic tool design.

ranked.headline: Peripheral and glial factors alter hippocampal and cortical neuronal function
ranked.summary: Recent mouse and culture studies link systemic and autoimmune insults to brain immune cells, astrocytes and neuronal excitability.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is how peripheral insults and autoantibodies reach brain immune cells, barrier function and glial signaling. Maternal TPOAb exposure in mice causes placental inflammation, fetal BBB disruption and hippocampal microglial activation. Kidney-derived osteopontin, cleaved by lung thrombin, drives hippocampal CCL2 upregulation and monocyte recruitment with delirium-like dysfunction after acute kidney injury. Neonatal SARS-CoV-2 spike exposure alters SOX2 and TBR1 populations regionally without broad BBB changes. Patient CASPR2 autoantibodies deplete the shed ectodomain, disrupting PMCA2 calcium regulation and network excitability. Newly, astrocyte-secreted Cathepsin D supports hippocampal LTP and memory through extracellular matrix remodeling.

ranked.headline: Cellular states linked to schizophrenia penetrance in 22q11.2 deletion carriers
ranked.summary: Recent preprints link penetrance-associated neuronal, glial and barrier differences to cellular states in 22q11.2 deletion carriers.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread across the 22q11.2-related items is cellular mechanism associated with variable schizophrenia penetrance in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome. In a deletion mouse model, prefrontal cortex at P28 shows increased immature and mature oligodendrocytes alongside reduced myelination. In iPSC-derived neurons from deletion carriers, schizophrenia is associated with impaired mitophagy and lysosomal acidity, a defect described as reversible. iPSC-derived blood-brain barrier cells from carriers display structural and metabolic differences linked to penetrance. What is new is the linkage of penetrance-associated differences to specific cellular states across neuronal, glial and barrier compartments. The cntnap2-/- autism study, which reports oligodendroglial dysfunction and parvalbumin interneuron hypomyelination, and the PLX5622 Purkinje cell and LKB1 granule cell studies address other models and are not attributed to the deletion.

ranked.headline: Transcriptional and post-transcriptional control of plant hormone pathways
ranked.summary: Recent studies map hormone-regulatory nodes to specific promoters, splice events and microRNA targets in stress and development.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is transcriptional and post-transcriptional control of hormone pathways. Several items target ABA: GhNAC029 represses GhNCED1 to reduce ABA synthesis and drought tolerance in cotton; methylation of the BraCYP707A3.A02 promoter blocks BraBPC2.A08 binding, altering ABA catabolism and clubroot resistance in Brassica; and SRPKII-mediated splicing of HAB1 shapes ABA sensitivity during Arabidopsis seedling establishment. ANAC030 promotes leaf senescence through JA biosynthesis, programmed cell death and chlorophyll metabolism. The miR159a-BrMYB12 module links myo-inositol and raffinose biosynthesis to heat tolerance in flowering Chinese cabbage. The maize H2A.Z study concerns chromatin distribution in leaf and endosperm and is peripheral to hormone signaling. What is new is the explicit mapping of hormone-regulatory nodes to specific promoters, splice events and microRNA targets.

ranked.headline: Sequence reconstruction methods increasingly target errors at their upstream source
ranked.summary: Recent preprints report reconstruction tools that control errors at source, from codon alignment to nanopore assembly and RNA search.
ranked.synthesis: Across these preprints, the common thread is that reconstruction and search steps are being redesigned to limit error propagation rather than correct errors downstream. WALRUS in HyPhy 3 estimates codon alignment, phylogeny and selection tests jointly, and is reported to reduce indel-driven false positives in simulated and avian data. HARICOT assembles raw nanopore signals without basecalling, using fuzzy de Bruijn graphs and Hough-transform overlap detection, and is reported to improve contiguity over comparators. TERRACE 2.0 combines outward paired-end and chimeric reads to assemble circular RNAs from short-read RNA-seq data. Infernal-GPU parallelizes covariance-model scoring on GPUs, recalibrates Rfam E-values and recovers remote structured RNA homologs missed by sequence filters. Two benchmarks examine upstream choices directly: local assembly consensus strategies depend on read type and error profile, and DNA polymerase selection affects HiFi assembly contiguity and completeness. What is new is the explicit evaluation of upstream decisions alongside method-level redesign.

ranked.headline: DNA repair and demethylation factors shape neurodevelopment and somatic L1 activity
ranked.summary: Recent preprints connect DNA repair factors, demethylation and somatic retrotransposition to neuronal gene expression and brain development.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is how DNA maintenance pathways intersect with neural gene regulation and brain development. In human cerebellar organoids, loss of TDP2 reduces PKA-CREB signalling and Purkinje cell maturation, and cAMP activation rescues growth. AAG competes with TDG for oxidized methylcytosine substrates, tuning active DNA demethylation, single-strand break formation and neuronal gene expression. LUSTRE, a single-cell assay, maps L1 insertion sites in about 17,600 adult human neurons to estimate somatic retrotransposition rates. Related preprints address murine SAMHD1 isoforms in replication fork dynamics, transposable element activity in aging visceral adipose tissue, and RepoV-based single-copy enhancer reporters in neural organoids. The new elements are mechanistic links between repair factors and signalling or demethylation, and single-cell resolution of somatic L1 activity in the human brain.

ranked.headline: Haplotype-resolved frameworks expose allele-specific, reference-dependent variation
ranked.summary: Haplotype-resolved and pangenome references now expose allele-specific expression and reference-dependent biological interpretation in crop genomes.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread across these preprints is that genotype-linked measurements depend on the genetic and reference framework used to interpret them. In potato, long-read RNA-seq resolves haplotype-specific expression, identifying a heat-inducible allele and a nucleus-targeted HSP40 isoform. A parent-of-origin-resolved Granny Smith genome shows that matched references reveal sun-exposure and cold-storage responses that other references miss. In Capsicum, a 48-genome super-pangenome links pungency and aroma terpene traits to Pun1 haplotypes and TPS genes, and a pangenome-guided k-mer GWAS maps signals onto a graph pangenome. Switchgrass field sampling across Michigan and Texas maps eQTL and GxE effects on regulation, while pearl millet ionomic stability under drought in Senegal relates to flowering and biomass. What is new is the use of haplotype-resolved and pangenome frameworks to resolve allele-specific and reference-dependent variation.

ranked.headline: SLC25A35 mediates mitochondrial import of branched-chain keto acids in metabolic tissues
ranked.summary: Five preprints connect mitochondrial carriers and fatty acid oxidation machinery to muscle, adipose, liver and cachexia phenotypes.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is that mitochondrial substrate entry and organelle remodeling set tissue metabolic output. Two preprints identify SLC25A35 as the mitochondrial carrier for branched-chain keto acids (BCKAs). One of them also names MCT1 and MCT2 as cellular entry transporters and reports that import limits hepatic BCKA handling; the other links BCKA uptake to adipocyte lipogenesis and fatty acid metabolism. MTCH2 supports mitochondrial metabolic remodeling, respiration and fatty acid oxidation in muscle satellite cells. Myeloid mDIC deletion shifts adipose macrophages toward an efferocytosis-associated state and preserves mitochondrial respiration. In KPC cachexia mice, muscle OPA1 overexpression or BNIP3 knockdown partly preserved muscle mass and function, sex-dependently. Dual Hadha and Hadhb mRNA delivery restores fatty acid oxidation in a trifunctional protein deficiency model. The new element is the transporter-level account of BCKA import.

ranked.headline: Joint modelling of mutational processes and variant consequences at sequence resolution
ranked.summary: Recent preprints couple multimodal mutational signatures and sequence-based mutation models with variant-level consequence assessment.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the joint modelling of mutation-generating processes and variant consequences at sequence resolution. MOTET infers multimodal mutational processes across SBS, DBS and indel signatures in 2,583 PCAWG cancer genomes, while EAGLE-MUT, a DNA language model trained on cancer mutation data, predicts somatic mutation probabilities that vary with sequence context and nucleosome positioning. A monoallelic MUTYH carrier shows the oxidative SBS18 signature across multiple normal tissues, suggesting a single hypomorphic allele. Variant-interpretation studies apply computational assessment to chromosome 21 base-editing accessibility and to TP63-IRF6-GRHL3 variants, and a CTSC structural analysis links predicted destabilization to ClinVar pathogenicity labels. What is new is the combination of several mutation classes and predictive sequence models with variant-level assessment. The items differ in scope and maturity, and all six are preprints, so this thread is dominant rather than shared by every item.

ranked.headline: Notch and SOX9 programs link neural progenitor maintenance to tissue architecture
ranked.summary: Quantitative 3D imaging of dorsal forebrain spheroids and organoid rosette studies now connect tissue architecture to progenitor regulatory programs.
ranked.synthesis: Across these items, the dominant thread is how signaling and epithelial architecture organize neural progenitors during early brain development. A SOX9-high radial glia program is reported to link progenitor maintenance to neuronal identity in cortical development, regulated by Notch and SOX9. Conditional loss of the Notch effector Rbpj in mice disrupts ventricular zone integrity and polarity, obstructing CSF flow and causing neonatal hydrocephalus. In human cortical organoids, neural rosettes are shown to arise from an interconnected tubular network formed by neuroepithelial folding and internalization. A whole-mount 3D imaging platform for dorsal forebrain spheroids detects altered growth and rosette phenotypes. The zebrafish meninges study, which implicates Foxc1 and Wnt, lies adjacent to this thread. What is new is the convergence of quantitative 3D tissue-scale analysis with defined regulatory programs.

ranked.headline: Trait lability and diversification rates vary across birds, lizards, legumes and insects
ranked.summary: Recent studies of birds, lizards, legumes and insects test how trait evolution couples with diversification and speciation.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread across these items is that phenotypic change proceeds unevenly and depends on demographic and ecological context rather than a single mechanism. In Mimosa, diversification rates form a continuum, with radiations accounting for most diversity and disparity and linked to abiotic niche lability. In island kingfishers, faster plumage color evolution tracks faster diversification and accelerates as genomic diversity declines, which the authors attribute to drift. In bark anoles, convergent signaling traits are decoupled from genomic species boundaries, with gene flow shaping speciation outcomes. Across 3,151 bird species, both Darwinian and Wallacean hypotheses explain sexual dichromatism in iridescence, and sexual dimorphism in leaf-footed bugs is labile. What is new is the explicit test of trait evolution against diversification, gene flow and genomic boundaries across independent lineages.

ranked.headline: Stress drives selective autophagy of organelles through distinct adaptors and tethers
ranked.summary: Recent work assigns specific adaptors, tethers and condensates to distinct stress contexts, from lysosomal damage to starvation and iron deficiency.
ranked.synthesis: Across these items, stress-responsive remodeling of organelles proceeds mainly through selective autophagy or related quality-control routes, although the compartments and stresses differ. Contact-phagy uses SIGMAR1-CCPG1 to turn over ER-mitochondria contact-site subdomains. The yeast ER-vacuole tether Mdm1 supports starvation-induced autophagy by balancing phospholipid and neutral lipid metabolism, enabling autophagosome completion. Iron deficiency triggers pexophagy through a GABARAP-FLCN/FNIP1 interaction that activates TFEB and TFE3. Processing bodies form during recovery from lysosomal damage and collaborate with stress granules to promote lysosomal quality and cell survival. RAB11 and RAB30 cooperate on endosomes under starvation, shear and osmotic stress, using phosphoinositide turnover to drive autophagy and survival. What is new is the assignment of specific adaptors, tethers and condensates to each stress context, rather than a single shared mechanism.

ranked.headline: Nuclear RNA maturation is governed by timing, composition and direct perturbation
ranked.summary: Fresh preprints and a J Cell Biol report add direct perturbation and phase-behavior data to nuclear RNA maturation timing.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that nuclear RNA maturation depends on the timing and molecular composition of processing steps. In Drosophila spermatocytes, Y-loop A co-transcriptional splicing is organized in chromatin hubs, with delays that vary by transcription cluster and increase as spermatocytes mature. In yeast, nuclear mRNPs share a minimal Yra1p/Pab1p core, while most factors associate transiently in stage-specific modules shaped by intron class and promoter. What is new is direct perturbation: the covalent molecular glue HL-1B stabilizes TOE1 binding to the spliceosome, altering snRNA 3'-processing and splicing in human cells. The zebrafish fractionation study links RNA insolubility to ribosome, poly(A) tail and m6A features, but addresses phase behavior rather than splicing, and the SF3b1 abscission work connects splicing to cytokinesis. The shared thread is therefore strongest for timing and composition rather than a unified mechanism.

ranked.headline: Senescent cells localize to spatial niches in aging adipose and liver tissue
ranked.summary: Recent preprints link senescent cells in aging human and mouse tissues to spatial niches and perturbation responses.
ranked.synthesis: The shared thread is that senescent cells in aging tissues are being resolved at cell-type and spatial scale. In human omental visceral adipose, older adults show more senescent cells than obesity alone explains, and senescent stem/progenitor and mesothelial cells participate in multicellular signaling that drives inflammation. In human liver, spatial transcriptomics places senescent SenSpots at portal tracts and fibrotic septa during metabolic liver disease progression. In aged mouse liver, senescent cells occupy inflammatory niches with distinct epigenetic senotypes, and p53 loss increases inflammation and metabolic damage, while MDM2 inhibitor-mediated p53 activation is reported to reverse age-linked changes. What is new is the combination of cell-type resolution, spatial context, and perturbation-linked evidence, although these findings derive from preprints and the perturbation evidence is limited to mouse liver.

ranked.headline: Shared latent structure is recovered from heterogeneous neural recordings
ranked.summary: Recent preprints show that heterogeneous neural recordings can be aligned and modeled to expose shared latent variables.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread across these five preprints is the recovery of shared latent structure from neural data that differ in session, subject, or recording format. Neuralign jointly aligns and decomposes heterogeneous recordings into shared tensor components, and Unified CEBRA pools recordings across sessions through a shared label to relate single-neuron contributions to population codes in mouse visual cortex. C3PO learns predictive, interpretable latent variables directly from unsorted, unbinned continuous-time spike trains. A digital twin of freely moving mouse V1 links classical tuning and behavioral gain effects to a general visual code, and in Drosophila, heterogeneous short-term plasticity across Kenyon cell inputs reformats temporal information into an explicit population clock. The studies do not address identical questions; what is new is the treatment of heterogeneity as structure to be modeled rather than noise to be removed.

ranked.headline: Chromatin responses to perturbation and enhancer rewiring across cell states
ranked.summary: Spatial, small-molecule and barcode-based chromatin profiling now links perturbations to accessibility, hub organization and enhancer rewiring.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread across these preprints is resolving how regulatory state responds to perturbation or cell-state change, using chromatin-level readouts. Perturb-Tags pairs spatially barcoded CRISPR perturbations with single-nucleus expression and chromatin accessibility, revealing non-autonomous transcriptomic and epigenomic responses. MolMap extends this to unmodified small molecules, profiling genome-wide accessibility changes in non-crosslinked nuclei and reporting early, compound-specific responses. On the mechanistic side, live imaging shows that hindsight transcription in response to Notch is sustained by a handover from Mastermind to Broad transcription hubs over time, while Hi-C and HiChIP across three differentiation systems show super-enhancers rewiring extensively. AMBER adds a mapping approach, linking accessible chromatin through hydrogel-assisted barcode seed expansion to multi-scale regulatory hubs in mouse brain cells. The new element is the combination of perturbation-resolved, spatially and temporally explicit chromatin readouts.

ranked.headline: Network and spatial structure shape how individual changes propagate to outcomes
ranked.summary: Simulation and theory studies now couple movement or social tie dynamics to demographic, epidemiological and evolutionary outcomes.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is that network or spatial topology determines how changes in individual animals or hosts propagate to population and community outcomes. Simulations across 268 empirical animal social networks show that compensatory tie formation alters how individual loss reorganises social structure, so predicted consequences of losing an individual depend on whether remaining animals rewire. Host-parasite coevolution on spatial networks links degree heterogeneity to host resistance and spatial variation in parasite infectivity. A spatially explicit individual-based model shows that herbivore movement and landscape structure jointly shape resource depletion and population dynamics. A theoretical model adds that parasite-impaired host mobility reduces virulence through altered relatedness and host density, with feedbacks on prevalence. What is new is the explicit coupling of movement or tie dynamics to evolutionary and demographic outcomes. These items are largely simulation- or theory-based, so the conclusions remain model-dependent pending empirical testing.

ranked.headline: Sound responses in aquatic animals vary by individual, life stage and season
ranked.summary: Preprints and an Arctic cod study show that sound responses in aquatic organisms depend on individual, developmental and seasonal state.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread across these items is intra-specific variation in how aquatic organisms respond to sound. In zebrafish, emergence latency differed among individuals and decreased across two tests, and sound exposure reduced vertical midline crossings more than ambient sound did. In Oikopleura dioica, anthropogenic noise altered behaviour in a life stage- and signal-dependent manner, with larvae appearing most sensitive. In Arctic cod, auditory evoked potential measurements revealed seasonal differences in hearing sensitivity between spawning and non-spawning fish. What is new is the explicit treatment of individual, life-stage and seasonal variation as features of sound responses rather than a single fixed response. The Arctic cod study is the only published item here; the zebrafish and Oikopleura work are preprints and should be treated as provisional.

ranked.headline: Estradiol-expanded Treg cells remodel maternal intestine; maternal cells reach neonates
ranked.summary: Mouse and goat studies now link hormonal control of intestinal immunity and lactation-stage tissue states to maternal-to-neonatal cell transfer.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is reproductive physiology reshaping maternal tissues and their immune compartments. In a mouse preprint, pregnancy-driven estradiol signaling expands intestinal regulatory T cells that secrete IL-10 and promote stem cell proliferation, remodeling the small intestine. A foster-nursing mouse preprint shows that maternal immune cells survive neonatal gut transit, enter circulation, and reach organs and injury sites in offspring. A single-cell and spatial transcriptomic preprint of Saanen goat mammary tissue across dry and peak lactation describes period-specific epithelial, stromal and immune changes. The goat study is descriptive profiling, and the transfer study concerns offspring rather than maternal remodeling, so the shared thread is partial. What is new is the joint attention to hormonal control of intestinal immune-epithelial remodeling, maternal-to-neonatal cell transfer, and lactation-stage mammary profiling.
